nodes.name: Er-doped NiFe-LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: One piece of Ni foam (NF) was placed into an inorganic salt mixed solution with NH₄F as the precipitant, and urea provided an alkaline environment. Ni foam acts as the substrate for the growth of LDH, as well as the current collector. After the hydrothermal treatment at 120°C for 12 h, the LDH sheet-like arrays were in situ growth on NF surface.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a illustrates the synthetic procedure for Er-NiFe-LDH@NF via a facile one-step hydrothermal method. Briefly, one piece of Ni foam (NF) was placed into an inorganic salt mixed solution with NH₄F as the precipitant, and urea provided an alkaline environment... After the hydrothermal treatment at 120°C for 12 h, the LDH sheet-like arrays were in situ growth on NF surface.

nodes.name: Er-free NiFe-LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe-LDH@NF was synthesized using the same one-step hydrothermal method but without Er(NO₃)₃ addition.
nodes.source_text: Er-free NiFe-LDH@NF sample reveals a similar architectural feature with Er-NiFe-LDH@NF (Figure S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: 2.5-Er-NiFe-LDH@NF Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Synthesized by adjusting the molar ratio of Er(NO₃)₃ in total metal ion content to 2.5%.
nodes.source_text: 2.5-Er-NiFe-LDH@NF, 5-Er-NiFe-LDH@NF and 7.5-Er-NiFe-LDH@NF were synthesized by adjusting the molar ratio of Er(NO₃)₃ in total metal ion content to 2.5%, 5% and 7.5%.

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 1.0 M KOH (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The optimized Er-NiFe-LDH@NF displays a significantly enhanced OER activity compared with NiFe-LDH@NF... The Er-NiFe-LDH@NF requires low overpotentials of only 192mV at 10mAcm⁻¹ and 240mV at 50mAcm⁻¹... A low Tafel slope of 51.1mVdec⁻¹ was observed in Er-NiFe-LDH@NF... The TOF value of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF at 280mV was calculated to be 0.588s⁻¹... the Ea value of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF was calculated to be 36.03kJ mol⁻¹

nodes.description: OER stability at 10 mA/cm² in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Chronopotentiometric (u-t) curves at the fixed current density of 10mAcm⁻² indicate that the Er-NiFe-LDH@NF presents the lower polarization tendency after 24h, in comparison with NiFe-LDH@NF and RuO₂

Figure 4b shows the multistep u-t curve for Er-NiFe-LDH@NF with tested current density increasing from 10 to 120mA cm⁻²... The potential promptly levels off at 1.49V for the start current value, and remains stable for 1h

nodes.description: CV stability after 3000 cycles in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the polarization curves of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF exhibits negligible decay before and after 3000 cyclic CV sweeps

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1 M KOH (two-electrode, Er-NiFe-LDH@NF || Pt/C)
nodes.source_text: the Er-NiFe-LDH@NF || Pt/C demands a low cell voltage of 1.43V at 10mAcm⁻²... the long-time overall water splitting measurement is carried out, which the current density of 12mAcm⁻¹ at 1.44V surpasses 12h with a negligible degradation of performance

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency for OER in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The obtained O₂ volume-time curve is close to the theoretical curve, demonstrating almost no side reaction during the water oxidation into oxygen.

nodes.description: Chronoamperometry at 1.6 V in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The chronoamperometric (i-t) curves at a fixed potential of 1.6V show that the current density of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF can stabilize at 100mA cm⁻² for 24h
NF exhibits no obvious electrocatalytic activity for OER, as shown in Figure 3a.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks match well with NiFe-LDH (PDF #40-0215), indicating well-maintained crystal structure after Er doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline structure of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF was explored by X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) in Figure 1b. The diffraction peaks located at 44.7°, 52.2°, and 76.3° correspond to the NF substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Er 4d signal at 169.5 eV confirms successful Er doping. Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ states; Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺ (711.20/724.27 eV) and Fe³⁺ (713.71/727.40 eV) species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The successful doping of Er species in NiFe-LDH was confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and Er 4d signal was observed at 169.5 eV (Figure 1c). For Ni 2p spectrum... two valence states of Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺... For Fe 2p spectrum, two peaks located at 711.20 and 724.27 eV are assignable to Fe²⁺ species... matched well with Fe³⁺ 2p.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type IV isotherms with H3 hysteresis loops; Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area of 28.64 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF is about 28.64 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Er doping facilitates OH⁻ adsorption on Ni site and promotes Ni(OH)₂ to NiOOH transformation, optimizing O₂ release kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical in-situ Raman spectra display that the Er dopants into NiFe-LDH can promote the transformation of Ni-OH into Ni-OOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Smaller semicircular diameter indicates lower charge transfer resistance (R_ct) and higher electronic conductivity vs NiFe-LDH@NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots in EIS analysis present that the semicircular diameter of Er-NiFe-LDH@NF is smaller than that of NiFe-LDH@NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: CVs at different scan rates used to calculate double layer capacitance C_dl = 2.0 mF/cm² for Er-NiFe-LDH@NF (vs 1.3 mF/cm² for NiFe-LDH@NF), indicating higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double layer capacitance (C_dl) was measured to evaluate the electrochemical active surface areas (ECSA)... The C_dl value for Er-NiFe-LDH@NF is 2.0 mF cm⁻² (Figure S17, Supporting Information), which is higher than that for NiFe-LDH@NF (1.3 mF cm⁻²).
